questions.question: If the message signal has a maximum frequency of 5 kHz, what is the required transmission bandwidth for an SSB-SC signal?

explanations.a: Correct! For SSB-SC, the bandwidth equals the message bandwidth, which is 5 kHz.
explanations.b: Incorrect! 10 kHz is the bandwidth for DSB-SC with the same message signal.
explanations.c: Incorrect! Bandwidth is not halved again.
explanations.d: Incorrect! 20 kHz is too large for a 5 kHz message signal.

questions.question: In SSB-SC modulation, why is only one sideband transmitted instead of both?

explanations.a: Incorrect! Power is not the main reason; the carrier is already suppressed.
explanations.b: Correct! Transmitting only one sideband halves the bandwidth compared to DSB-SC, making it more efficient.
explanations.c: Incorrect! Carrier amplitude is not affected by sideband selection.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Coherent detection is still required for demodulation.

questions.question: Which sideband does SSB-SC transmit if the upper sideband (USB) is selected?

answers.d: No sideband; only carrier is transmitted

explanations.a: Incorrect! This describes LSB, not USB.
explanations.b: Incorrect! SSB transmits only one sideband.
explanations.c: Correct! USB corresponds to the higher frequency sideband above the carrier.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Carrier is suppressed in SSB-SC.

questions.question: A message signal has a maximum frequency of 4 kHz. If we generate an SSB-SC signal using a carrier of 100 kHz, what will be the frequency range of the upper sideband?

explanations.a: Correct! Upper sideband ranges from carrier (100 kHz) to carrier + message max (100 + 4).
explanations.b: Incorrect! 96–100 kHz corresponds to the lower sideband.
explanations.c: Incorrect! 108 kHz is beyond the actual USB range.
explanations.d: Incorrect! This is not related to the USB.

questions.question: In DSB-SC demodulation, what is the effect of a phase mismatch between the transmitter and receiver carrier signals?

answers.a: It changes the frequency of the output signal without affecting amplitude.
answers.b: It reduces output amplitude and introduces distortion.
answers.c: It has no effect if the signal amplitude is high.

explanations.a: Incorrect! Amplitude is affected, not frequency alone.
explanations.b: Correct! Phase mismatch reduces amplitude and causes distortion in the recovered signal.
explanations.c: Incorrect! Amplitude alone cannot correct phase mismatch effects.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Phase mismatch reduces, not increases, effective signal power.

questions.question: Which component is essential in SSB-SC modulation to generate a phase-shifted version of the message signal?

explanations.a: Incorrect! A balanced amplifier does not create a phase-shifted signal.
explanations.b: Correct! The Hilbert transform produces a 90° phase-shifted version required for SSB-SC.
explanations.c: Incorrect! Low-pass filters remove high-frequency components but do not phase-shift.
explanations.d: Incorrect! PLLs are used for carrier synchronization, not phase-shifting the message.

questions.question: In SSB-SC modulation, what is the role of the Hilbert transform of the message signal?

answers.b: It generates a 90° phase-shifted version of the message signal to create a single sideband.
answers.c: It reduces the message bandwidth by half.
answers.d: It directly recovers the message signal at the receiver.

explanations.a: Incorrect! Carrier suppression is handled by the modulator, not the Hilbert transform.
explanations.b: Correct! The Hilbert transform produces a quadrature signal used to generate only one sideband.
explanations.c: Incorrect! The bandwidth is reduced by transmitting only one sideband, not by the Hilbert transform itself.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Message recovery is done by coherent detection at the receiver.

questions.question: In SSB-SC systems, what is the main challenge in achieving perfect carrier suppression?

answers.c: Low power of the transmitted signal.
answers.d: Maintaining precise oscillator frequency and phase, and handling non-ideal components.

explanations.a: Incorrect! Bandwidth is not the main factor.
explanations.b: Incorrect! Amplifier non-linearities are secondary concerns.
explanations.c: Incorrect! Signal power alone does not determine carrier suppression quality.
explanations.d: Correct! Perfect suppression requires precise oscillator control and good component performance.

questions.question: In SSB-SC demodulation, how does noise affect phase detection?

answers.b: Noise affects only amplitude, not phase.
answers.c: Noise causes phase jitter, reducing demodulation fidelity.
answers.d: Noise has no effect if SNR is high.

explanations.b: Incorrect! Noise affects both amplitude and phase.
explanations.c: Correct! Noise can cause phase jitter and degrade the recovered signal.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Even high SNR cannot completely eliminate phase errors caused by noise.

questions.question: Calculate the transmitted power of a DSB-SC signal if the message signal is a sinusoid with a peak amplitude of 2 V and is transmitted over a 1 Ω resistive load. (Assume a normalized carrier amplitude of 1 V).

explanations.a: Incorrect! 2 W is the power of the message signal P_m = A_m^2 / 2R. Due to modulation, DSB-SC power is half of this.
explanations.b: Correct! DSB-SC power is calculated as P_DSB = P_m / 2. Since P_m = 2 W, the transmitted power is 1 W.
explanations.c: Incorrect! This value ignores the factor of 1/2 introduced by the carrier multiplication process.
explanations.d: Incorrect! 0.5 W would be the power of an SSB-SC signal, which contains only one sideband. DSB-SC contains both, so it is 1 W.
